links.outcome: Readability of LLM counseling outputs by readability indices
links.effect: Four readability indices (e.g., Flesch Kincaid Grade Level) indicated college graduation would be required to understand every counseling output; too much medical (49%) and non-medical (45%) terminology.
links.quote: Four readability indices (e.g., Flesch Kincaid Grade Level) consistently indicated that college graduation would be required to understand every counseling output.

links.outcome: Appropriate communication of urgency in LLM counseling for high-urgency retinal vignettes
links.effect: Counseling urgency did not differ from clinical urgency except for high-urgency AMD (p = 0.013) and high-urgency RD (p < 0.001); urgency differed between high/low DR (p < 0.001).
links.quote: Counseling urgency did not differ significantly from clinical urgency of all vignettes, except for the high-urgency AMD (p = 0.013) and high-urgency RD (p < 0.001).

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT-3.5's performance in generating ophthalmic counseling across simulated patient vignettes with expert ophthalmologist grading, without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail intervention.
